Title: A man died. Why the laughing emoji?
Article:
LETTERS:
There is something profoundly unsettling about opening a news report announcing that a motorcyclist has died — only to find laughing emojis underneath it.
A man is dead. Somewhere, a family has received a telephone call that will change their lives forever. Yet strangers who never knew him respond with laughter, sarcasm or variations of "padan muka".
Have Malaysians become heartless?
Perhaps the more difficult question is: what happened before that emoji was clicked?
The fatal crash reported today involved a 38-year-old Yamaha RXZ rider on the LPT2 near Ajil-Telemong.
According to the police account reported by the media, two motorcycles are believed to have sideswiped each other before falling. A car approaching from behind then struck one of the riders, throwing him into a drain. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act.
That distinction matters.
We should not automatically label this particular deceased rider a Mat Rempit, nor conclude that he was performing a stunt.
An RXZ is a motorcycle model, not a diagnosis of its rider's character.
But the public reaction to his death cannot be separated from the wider social context surrounding reckless motorcycle behaviour.
WHEN EMPATHY RUNS LOW
For years, Malaysians have watched videos of riders weaving through traffic, travelling in huge convoys, racing illegally, blocking roads and performing the notorious "Superman" position.
So the public anxiety is not entirely imaginary.
But something psychologically significant happens when fear and frustration are repeated often enough.
Fear becomes frustration.
Frustration becomes anger.
Anger becomes resentment.
And resentment can eventually make empathy conditional.
That, I believe, is what we are beginning to witness.
FROM HUMAN BEING TO LABEL
There is a psychological phenomenon known as deindividuation, where we stop seeing the individual and begin seeing only the group.
The deceased is no longer a father, husband, son, brother, colleague or friend.
He becomes simply: "Rempit".
Once that happens, our moral relationship with him changes.
We begin to reason, consciously or otherwise, that because people in that group knowingly take risks, they deserve whatever happens to them.
Malaysia does have a genuine motorcycle safety crisis.
In 2025, 6,537 people died on Malaysian roads, with motorcyclists and pillion riders accounting for about 66 per cent of the deaths. The Government has targeted a 50 per cent reduction in road fatalities by 2030.
The recent RXZ phenomenon has sharpened the debate further.
A road safety advocate recently highlighted an increase in fatalities associated with the annual RXZ Members programme — from two in 2024 to five in 2025 and 11 in 2026 — while calling for comprehensive risk management around such mass gatherings.
These numbers should concern us far more than the brand of motorcycle somebody rides.
Because behind every statistic is precisely what we risk forgetting when we press that laughing emoji:
A human being.
So, are we becoming heartless?
I don't think that is the whole story.
I think our collective empathy is suffering from fatigue.
People become less compassionate when they repeatedly perceive others as knowingly creating danger and expecting society to absorb the consequences.
But empathy fatigue can become dangerous in its own right.
Today, it is the Mat Rempit.
Tomorrow, it could be the speeding driver, the drunk driver, the jaywalker, the drug addict, the smoker or anyone else whose behaviour we have come to associate with risk or irresponsibility.
Somebody's death should never become entertainment simply because we disapprove of the group to which we believe he belongs.
Perhaps the most important lesson from these reactions is therefore not about RXZ riders at all.
It is about us.
We need enforcement without hatred. Education without condescension. Consequences without humiliation.
And where thrill-seeking, peer pressure and a desire for belonging drive dangerous behaviour, we need legitimate environments and interventions capable of redirecting that energy — rather than pretending enforcement alone will erase the psychology behind it.
At the same time, riders themselves must understand something equally fundamental:
Public empathy is not limitless.
Every Superman stunt performed among innocent motorists, every illegal race, every dangerous convoy and every deliberate disregard for another road user's safety takes another withdrawal from society's reservoir of goodwill.
Eventually, that reservoir can run dry.
And perhaps that is what those laughing emojis are really telling us.
Not necessarily that Malaysians have suddenly become cruel.
But that too many Malaysians have become tired of being frightened by someone else's idea of fun.
We should be deeply concerned about that.
Because the answer cannot be a choice between road safety and humanity.
A mature society must insist upon both.
Condemn the behaviour. Punish the offence. Protect innocent road users.
But when a life ends, remember that beneath the helmet was still somebody's son, father, brother or friend.
We should never need a laughing emoji to make the case for safer roads.
The writer, Syed Mohammed Idid Syed Ahmed Idid is a  highway safety advocate, a father and husband who wishes we all get home safely at the end of the day.

Title: September 'real battleground' for Indonesia in fight against forest fires as el Nino peaks
Article:
JAKARTA: September will be Indonesia's "real battleground" in the fight against forest and land fires as El Nino reaches its peak, with the country still facing significant risks despite a decline in fire hotspots following a month of intensified firefighting efforts.
Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said the government was using the severe 2015 El Nino as a benchmark, with this year's phenomenon of comparable strength, although about 202,004ha had been burned as of July, compared with some 600,000ha over the same period in 2015.
"September is the peak of El Nino. Thank God the trend is declining and we must maintain it, but we must remain vigilant, extremely vigilant, because for me, September is the real battleground.
"We have not yet emerged from the El Nino threat. We are not safe at all yet," he told a press conference streamed live on Tuesday, adding that the August burned-area figure was still being calculated, including through drone checks to ensure accuracy.
Raja Juli said five measures would remain central to the government's efforts in September: weather modification operations (OMC), water bombing, ground firefighting, law enforcement and greater public awareness.
The government has deployed 53 air assets for patrols, OMC and water bombing, with assistance from Japan expected and Russian aircraft leased by BNPB set to be deployed to South Sumatra in the coming weeks.
On enforcement, Raja Juli said police had named 89 suspects in forest and land fire cases, while the Forestry Ministry was processing 30 criminal cases and had issued warnings to 52 forest utilisation business permit (PBPH) holders, six of whom had been subjected to severe sanctions.
He said Indonesia would continue its efforts to minimise the impact of transboundary haze on neighbouring countries.

Title: Rauf becomes delivery rider for a day
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh stepped into the shoes of a p-hailing rider, collecting food orders and delivering them to customers' homes to experience firsthand the daily routine of those working in the sector.
The experience was aimed at helping him better understand the challenges faced by p-hailing riders who earn a living through various digital platforms.
Rauf said he appreciated the dedication of the riders, who work hard every day to support their families, and wanted to see for himself how they receive orders, collect food and make deliveries.
"I tried to become one of the delivery riders and learn how they receive orders. After that, I tried delivering the food to customers' homes.
"I really appreciate the income they earn to support their families at home," he said when met by reporters after engaging with p-hailing riders at Masjid Tanah Sentral today.
He said the role of p-hailing riders should be given due attention as they also contributed to the country's economic growth through online delivery services.
He said changes in technology and people's lifestyles had also transformed business and economic practices, making the role of p-hailing riders increasingly important.
"I believe they need to be viewed from various perspectives, and I will recommend that the relevant authorities look into their welfare.
"They contribute to the economy and the government in Malaysia," he said.
Meanwhile, Rauf said more than
3,000 p-hailing riders in Melaka
were expected to benefit from assistance being formulated, with details to be announced soon.
He also invited p-hailing riders to attend the Karnival Anak Muda at MITC on Sept 4, which will feature a lucky draw offering 10 motorcycles and special-edition helmets bearing the chief minister's branding.
Earlier, Rauf delivered food to a customer's home in the Pengkalan Balak area before ending his ride in Pekan Masjid Tanah.

Title: Father mulls legal action after son dies from suspected electrocution at futsal court
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: The father of a 15-year-old boy who died after he was believed to have been electrocuted at a futsal court in Bestari Jaya is considering legal action over alleged negligence.
Norramin Senin, 49, said that although he did not wish to blame any party, he hoped his son, Muhammad Anas Muazim, would be the last victim.
"I accept Allah's will. Let my son be the only victim, and I hope no one else suffers the same fate," said the lorry driver.
In the 10pm incident last night, the Form Three student was believed to have
touched a lamp post
suspected of carrying an electric current while resting during a futsal game, causing him to collapse.
"The place is used by many people regardless of age, race or religion. I do not want to accuse anyone, but this involves negligence that ended with the loss of a life," he said when met at his home in Taman Seri Indah, Bestari Jaya, today.
Earlier, Anas was laid to rest at the Bestari Jaya Muslim cemetery at about 3pm.
Recalling the incident, Norramin said his son returned home at about 8pm, had dinner and prepared to perform Isyak prayers at the mosque before heading to the nearby futsal court with his friends.
At about 10pm, one of the victim's friends contacted Norramin's second child to inform the family that Anas had collapsed.
"I immediately rushed to the location and found my son being supported by his friends.
"Seeing that he was unconscious, I asked them to lay him down and contacted a friend to call an ambulance. I performed CPR several times, but I had a feeling that his chances were already 50-50.
"But Allah loved him more," said Norramin.
He said he briefly returned home to inform his wife, Jamiatulhuda Ishak, 44, before going back to the scene, where medical personnel were performing CPR on his son.
"Unfortunately, he was already gone.
"He had shown no changes in his behaviour and went about his daily routine as usual. He had even helped his uncle, who held a wedding reception last Saturday.
"He was a cheerful boy who loved joking with his siblings and was friendly with everyone in the community. Wherever he went, people knew him," he said.
Meanwhile, Kuala Selangor police chief Superintendent Azaharudin Tajudin said investigations found that the victim had touched a lamp post suspected of carrying an electric current before collapsing.
He said an examination found no elements of foul play, while the cause of death was recorded as "consistent with electrocution".
The case has been classified as sudden death.

Title: Seni Jaya unit bags seven-year RTS Link advertising concession
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seni Jaya Corp Bhd's unit SJX Media Sdn Bhd has clinched a seven-year advertising media concession for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link (RTS Link).
SJX Media entered into an advertising concession agreement with Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS) on Sept 1 for the design, build, operation and transfer of advertising media facilities for the RTS Link.
Under the agreement, SJX Media will have exclusive rights to design, procure, manufacture, install, test, commission, operate and maintain advertising media at designated spaces within the RTS Link.
It will also be responsible for marketing, managing and generating revenue from the advertising spaces throughout the concession period.
The concession will run for seven years from the commencement date, with MRTS having the option to extend it for another three years on mutually agreed terms.
Before operations begin, SJX Media will undertake the required planning, design, approvals, procurement, fabrication, installation, testing and commissioning works at its own cost.
The pre-operational works must be completed within three months from the date the agreement becomes legally effective.
Once operations begin, SJX Media will make payments to MRTS, including a minimum annual guarantee and revenue-sharing payments under the agreement.
"The agreement is expected to contribute positively to the future earnings, earnings per share, net assets per share and gearing of the company.
"It will not have any effect on the share capital and the shareholding of the substantial shareholders of the company," Seni Jaya said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
SJX Media, incorporated in October 2025, is 70 per cent owned by Seni Jaya Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Seni Jaya. The remaining 30 per cent is held by Southern XMedia Sdn Bhd.
MRTS is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd. It was established to undertake the construction of the RTS Link and related commercial activities at the station, including advertising space.

Title: MACC strengthens global cooperation against cross-border corruption
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has stepped up international cooperation in tackling cross-border corruption through its participation in the seventh plenary meeting of the Global Operational Network of Anti-Corruption Law Enforcement Authorities (GlobE Network).
The meeting was held from Aug 25 to 28 at the Vienna International Centre in Austria.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the platform enabled bilateral and multilateral discussions, the sharing of knowledge and developments, and cooperation on cross-border cases.
"Direct cooperation and the rapid, informal exchange of information between member authorities are crucial in supporting investigations, particularly when cases involve financial transactions, assets or individuals overseas," he said in a statement today.
Abd Halim said this was MACC's fourth participation since joining the network in May 2023, reflecting its continued commitment to international cooperation in cross-border corruption investigations, tracing illicit financial flows and asset recovery.
"The meeting covered the latest developments within the GlobE Network, its 2025 activity report, and the use of artificial intelligence and technology in corruption investigations.
"Members also discussed efforts to strengthen the network's performance, financial sustainability and strategic direction," he said.
Abd Halim said 20 GlobE Network authorities had signed a model agreement on information exchange, including agencies from Saudi Arabia, Chile, Ukraine, Romania and South Africa.
"The agreement is an important step towards strengthening direct and secure information-sharing mechanisms among network members," he said.
MACC Intelligence Division Senior Director Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin also shared Malaysia's experience in handling cross-border corruption cases, including those involving offshore jurisdictions, during a panel session titled "Following the Money: Fake Invoices and Offshore Trails" on Aug 26.
Abd Halim said Saiful Ezral highlighted legal and evidential challenges in obtaining information and evidence from overseas while meeting the requirements of different jurisdictions.
Abd Halim also led bilateral meetings with authorities from Mauritius, the United Kingdom, China, Mongolia, Syria, Ukraine and Kuwait to discuss ongoing cases and explore potential areas of cooperation.

Title: Ta Win unit to slash workforce by 52pct in cost-cutting move
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ta Win Holdings Bhd's subsidiary Ta Win Industries (M) Sdn Bhd will cut 39 jobs, or 52 per cent of its workforce, as part of a cost-cutting exercise.
In a bourse filing, Ta Win said the exercise will begin on Sept 11 as it seeks to streamline operations, remove redundant positions and reduce costs amid current market conditions.
The company said the exercise will result in one-off restructuring costs that are expected to have a material impact on its earnings for the financial year ending June 30, 2027.
However, Ta Win expects the job cuts to deliver longer-term cost savings and improve operational efficiency.
Affected employees will be provided with career counselling and job placement assistance, it said.

Title: From RM120 website to RM4mil in coffee sales
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A RM120 investment in a website helped local coffee entrepreneur Mirwan Badri Ahmad Badri turn a pandemic setback into nearly RM4 million in sales within two years.
Mirwan Badri, 41, said his online marketplace, Buna Market, was launched in January 2020 to harness digital technology as Malaysia imposed movement restrictions during the Covid-19 pandemic.
"The cost of setting up the Buna Market website was about US$29, or roughly RM120. In January 2020, our sales were around RM3,000 to RM4,000 before rising to RM5,000 to RM6,000 in February.
"In March 2020, the government shut down businesses following the outbreak of Covid-19. But our sales jumped to about RM40,000 in April 2020 as people could no longer leave their homes and turned to online shopping," he said in a recent interview.
The surge prompted him to approach coffee-machine distributors and roasters, inviting them to sell their products through Buna Market.
"Alhamdulillah, Buna Market started with just 20 SKUs (stock-keeping units), but the number of products listed on our website eventually peaked at 2,000. Within two years, our sales had almost reached RM4 million," he said.
Mirwan Badri said the experience showed that building a successful business did not necessarily require substantial capital, but making the most of existing relationships could open doors.
"I had already known the distributors of machines, grinders and coffee equipment since I started my business. We always maintained good relationships and built trust, which made them comfortable letting us sell their products. Some distributors even offered to place their products with us on consignment.
"This made it easier for us to sell high-value products while also providing servicing and installation for customers," he said.
FROM SETBACK TO COMEBACK
Mirwan Badri started his coffee business in 2013 after leaving a career in corporate banking. His interest in the food industry was sparked while working at Pret A Manger in London after completing a master's degree in mechanical engineering.
His entrepreneurial journey was far from smooth. He said he came close to bankruptcy twice, including after the closure of an outlet in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (Kuala Lumpur) in 2019.
The outlet lasted just six months, leaving him with a RM350,000 loss and forcing him to reduce his workforce from 17 employees to three. His coffee-supply business was also hit after several major customers were lost.
"Of course, I can't lie, there were many times when I felt like giving up. But whenever I felt that way, I would call my mother, talk to my wife and share my problems with my friends.
"Most people, when we share honestly and don't hide how we feel, genuinely want to help. If they cannot help financially, they may be able to offer words of encouragement," he said.
Mirwan Badri owns Sprezzatura Sdn Bhd and Sprezzatura Coffee in Phileo Damansara, Petaling Jaya, Selangor. He also runs Coffee Marketplace, which focuses on trading green coffee beans, and Utan Kopi, a premium brand featuring locally grown coffee.
His story is among 69 micro-entrepreneur stories featured in Bank Simpanan Nasional's (BSN) 'Cerita Mereka, Jiwa Malaysia' campaign in conjunction with Malaysia's 69th National Day celebrations.
Mirwan Badri also received RM50,000 in financing under BSN Micro-i Madani, which he applied for during the pandemic to help revive his business.
The financing helped him introduce new products, buy furniture, upgrade coffee machines and strengthen working capital.
He said the financing played an important role in keeping his business afloat during a difficult period.
Meanwhile, BSN chief operating officer Zarir Mohd Rawi said more than 5,000 micro-entrepreneurs had benefited from BSN Micro-i Madani so far this year, bringing the total number of recipients to 180,000 since the scheme was introduced in 2007.
"The scheme offers financing ranging from RM2,000 to RM100,000. In general, it aims to help micro-entrepreneurs grow their businesses, whether by starting a new venture or expanding an existing one," he said.

Title: Five-sen coin's future hangs in balance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Coins of various denominations have long been widely used in everyday transactions.
However, the rise of digital payments has gradually eroded the role of coins in daily life.
As the use of coins continues to decline, questions are being raised over whether the five-sen coin remains relevant.
Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the use of five sen coins has declined, but there is still demand for them, particularly in the retail sector.
"We want to ensure inclusivity, so we need to meet the demand as long as there is still a need to use five sen coins.
"So, we will continue to issue five sen coins for now and monitor the situation based on the needs of the economy," he said in an interview with BuletinTV3.
[[nid:1523704]]
Malaysian Retailers Association (MRA) president Datuk Andrew Lim Tatt Keong, meanwhile, expressed concern that withdrawing five sen coins from circulation could lead to higher prices for goods, effectively reducing consumers' purchasing power.
"So, will there come a day when we no longer have 20 sen coins and only use 50 sen coins?
"Then, perhaps one day, the 50 sen coin could also be discontinued, leaving us to use only ringgit denominations.
"In such a situation, there would be a tendency for costs to rise because smaller coin or cash denominations would no longer be available," he said.
[[nid:1523703]]
HELP University economist Prof. Chung Tin Fah, however, takes a different view, arguing that the five-sen coin no longer offers significant economic value.
"You can still price something at five sen, but we no longer need the physical coin.
"There would be no inflationary impact because payments could still be made through e-wallets. It is only the physical five-sen coin that would no longer be available," he said.
He also believes that the cost of producing five sen coins is higher than their face value.
[[nid:1523702]]
Meanwhile, Bank Negara Malaysia Numismatic Gallery curator Wan Muhammad Danial Wan Omar said Malaysian coins had undergone three major changes or evolutions since they were first introduced in 1967.
"The evolution of Malaysian coins has shown a trend towards smaller sizes and lighter weights to reduce production costs. Secondly, this improves efficiency in terms of handling," he said.
He said the first and second series of Malaysian coins comprised six denominations, ranging from one sen to one dollar and one ringgit.
However, the one sen and one ringgit coins were withdrawn from circulation in 2012, leaving the Third Series, which remains in use today, with only four denominations.

Title: Forecast: Indonesian fire pollutants potentially moving towards Malaysia
Article:
JAKARTA: Pollutants from fires in Indonesia's Sumatra and Kalimantan are continuing to move towards the Strait of Malacca and Natuna Sea, and potentially towards Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei, according to a forecast presented by Indonesian authorities on Tuesday.
The forecast by Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) came as fire spots declined sharply across priority provinces in Kalimantan and remained relatively low in Sumatra on Tuesday, although severe air pollution persisted in parts of both islands.
National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Acting Head of Data, Information and Disaster Communication Centre Berton Panjaitan said Central Kalimantan recorded the highest number at 63, down from 72 a day earlier, while West Kalimantan fell to 30 from 104 and South Kalimantan to 13 from 55.
In Sumatra, he told an online press conference on Tuesday that Riau recorded four fire spots, while Jambi and South Sumatra had 13 each, with the latter edging up from 11 a day earlier.
According to data displayed during the press conference, air pollution remained severe in parts of Kalimantan, with the Air Pollutant Standard Index (ISPU) reaching 680 in Katingan, Central Kalimantan, 468 in Southeast Pontianak, West Kalimantan and 405 in Murung Raya, Central Kalimantan, as of 4.09pm local time.
"Visibility remained below 1km in West Kalimantan, about two kilometres in Central Kalimantan and below three kilometres in South Kalimantan," Berton said.
In Sumatra, he said air quality had improved, particularly in Riau and Jambi, while conditions in South Sumatra were generally moderate, though visibility there remained below 2km.
"Normal activities, including face-to-face learning, have continued in Riau, with visibility improving to more than 9km. Car Free Day was also held last Sunday, which shows that air quality, particularly in Pekanbaru, has improved. We hope these conditions will continue," he said.
Berton said ground teams had extinguished fires covering about 263ha in West Kalimantan, 87ha in Central Kalimantan and 29ha in South Kalimantan.
"In Sumatra, the figures were more than 126ha in Riau, 13ha in Jambi and 9.25ha in South Sumatra as of Monday.
"Even after the fire has been extinguished, the work is not over, as the area still has to be wetted and cooled until there is no remaining heat. Peatland fires pose extraordinary challenges compared with vegetation fires on mineral soil," he said.
Regarding weather modification operations, Berton said light to moderate rain was observed in parts of Jambi after 2,000kg of salt were dispersed, while an operation in Central Kalimantan failed to produce rain.
Similar efforts could not be conducted in Riau, South Sumatra and South Kalimantan due to a lack of suitable clouds, he said.

Title: Alam Maritim to buy RM81mil OSV as subsea business expands
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alam Maritim Resources Bhd plans to acquire a newly built offshore support vessel (OSV) for US$19.8 million (RM80.8 million) to expand its subsea operations and support its RM1.55 billion order book.
The proposed acquisition will be undertaken through subsidiary Alam Maritim (M) Sdn Bhd (AMSB), which entered into a vessel purchase option agreement with Singapore-based Poet Shipbuilding & Engineering Pte Ltd on Dec 1, 2025.
Under the agreement, AMSB paid an option fee of US$900,000 (RM3.67 million) for the right to purchase the vessel.
The option, initially due to expire on July 31, 2026, was extended twice through addendums dated July 31 and Aug 21, 2026. It now expires on Oct 31, 2026.
Alam Maritim said its board intends to exercise the option and proceed with the acquisition, subject to shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting.
Upon approval, AMSB and Poet will enter into a definitive shipbuilding contract for the construction and delivery of the vessel.
The contract is expected to take effect on Nov 1, 2026, with delivery targeted within 24 months, or by October 2028.
The 65-metre OSV will have accommodation for 80 people and a deck cargo capacity of about 300 tonnes, as well as crane capabilities.
It will be powered by two 1,678-kilowatt main engines and classified by the American Bureau of Shipping.
Alam Maritim said the vessel would be deployed for its subsea engineering services, including remotely operated vehicle and saturation diving operations.
"With the proposed OSV acquisition, the group will operate a total of five OSVs, out of which four are under bareboat or time charter, which will enhance the group's operational capabilities and strengthen its position within the subsea services segment," it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The acquisition is aimed at increasing Alam Maritim's capacity to undertake more subsea projects, broaden its customer base and reduce its reliance on third-party vessel charters.
The subsea segment generated RM415.4 million, or 86.72 per cent, of Alam Maritim's RM479.04 million revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2025.
As at June 30, 2026, the segment had an estimated remaining contract value and secured order book of RM1.55 billion, which is expected to support earnings through 2029.
Alam Maritim said it opted for a new vessel due to the limited availability of suitable second-hand OSVs and the need to meet clients' specifications and vessel-age requirements.
The RM80.8 million purchase consideration will be funded equally through internal funds and bank borrowings, with RM40.4 million from each source.
Another RM4.26 million is expected to be incurred for sailing, maintenance and handling expenses.
The US$900,000 option fee will be credited against the first instalment of the purchase price.
Assuming RM40.4 million in bank financing, Alam Maritim's gearing is expected to rise to 0.50 times from 0.02 times on a pro forma basis.
If the required approvals are not obtained by Oct 31, 2026, the option agreement will lapse and Poet may retain the option fee.
The proposed acquisition comes less than three months after Alam Maritim exited PN17 status on June 8, 2026, following a debt restructuring and regularisation plan that ended its four-year stint under the classification.

Title: Kee Ming clinches RM40mil M&E jobs in Penang, Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kee Ming Group Bhd's unit Kee Ming Electrical Sdn Bhd has secured two subcontracts worth a combined RM40 million for mechanical and electrical (M&E) engineering works at industrial projects in Penang and Selangor.
The first subcontract, worth RM21 million, involves works for a warehouse in the Valdor Industrial Area, Penang.
The scope includes the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of air-conditioning and mechanical ventilation (ACMV), fire protection, electrical, telephone and extra-low voltage services, as well as building management systems.
The project is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
The second subcontract, valued at RM19 million, covers electrical services, fire protection and ACMV systems for a warehouse at Taman Perdagangan Elmina, Selangor.
It is scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2027.
Both subcontracts were awarded by a third-party contractor involved in the design, supply and installation of steel structures, as well as civil engineering and building construction.
Kee Ming said the fixed-price, lump-sum contracts also include infrastructure works within the project boundaries, street lighting and card access systems, where applicable.
Managing director Ir Liew Kar Hoe said the awards strengthened Kee Ming's industrial project pipeline and reflected the breadth of its M&E engineering capabilities.
He said the scope of works demonstrated the company's ability to deliver integrated solutions for industrial developments.
Liew said the industrial segment remained an important market for the group, with the latest awards broadening its exposure across key locations in Penang and Selangor.
"Our priority is to execute these projects well, maintain cost discipline and continue building a diversified pipeline across industrial, commercial, clean energy and infrastructure opportunities," he said.
As at June 30, 2026, Kee Ming's outstanding order book stood at RM206.4 million.
The company said it was expanding its project teams and operational systems to support a larger and more diverse portfolio of M&E engineering projects.

Title: Global bond sell-off deepens on inflation concerns
Article:
LONDON: A global bond sell-off deepened on Tuesday, pushing government borrowing costs higher and equities lower as investors worried that energy-driven inflation could force central banks to raise interest rates.
The latest escalation in fighting between the United States and Iran has sent oil prices higher, stoking concerns that tighter monetary policy could weigh on economic growth.
Heavy selling pushed the interest rate on 30-year UK government bonds to its highest since 1998, while the 10-year yield rose to a level not seen since the 2007-08 global financial crisis.
Japan's 10-year government bond yield touched a 30-year high of three per cent, reflecting concerns over plans for massive government spending.
The yield on the 30-year US Treasury bond stood at 5.27 per cent, not far from levels last seen in 2007, while the 10-year yield rose to its highest level since January 2025.
"The bond sell-off has... been a global affair," said Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid.
He said the "main culprit was the weekend escalation in the Middle East that saw the US and Iran exchange strikes for the first time since late July".
European stocks tumbled, with Frankfurt shedding more than one per cent and London also falling as trading resumed after a public holiday.
Official data showed that eurozone inflation hit a three-year high of 3.3 per cent in August, cementing expectations that the European Central Bank would raise interest rates next week.
Oil prices jumped around two per cent on Tuesday after the US and Iran traded fire for the first time in weeks, and US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "hard".
After six months of war, the conflict remains at an impasse, with Tehran keeping the strategic Strait of Hormuz closed and Washington maintaining a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
"With Trump now threatening further action against Iran, including against Kharg Island, Iran's key oil export hub, supply worries are once again front and centre," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
Traders are now awaiting key economic data ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Sept 16.
The jobs and consumer price index reports could play a major role in whether the bank lifts rates, with bets on an increase surging after Fed chair Kevin Warsh gave a hawkish speech on Friday.
Asian stock markets on Tuesday followed Wall Street lower, with Tokyo, Hong Kong and Shanghai all falling.
The yen weakened against the dollar despite US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent telling CNBC he expected Japan to support the currency, which has lost half the gains made in a historic joint intervention after it hit a 40-year low.
The comments were seen as a signal for the Bank of Japan to tighten monetary policy when it meets this month.
In company news, shares in fast-fashion giant Shein slumped 10 per cent at one point on its long-awaited Hong Kong trading debut, having raised US$1.7 billion in a high-profile initial public offering.
It later pared the losses to close almost flat.
Shares in Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek soared nearly 10 per cent after US tech giant Nvidia announced it had injected US$3.5 billion into the company.

Title: Malaysians advised to stay vigilant following Mount Sinabung eruption
Article:
JAKARTA: Malaysians in or travelling to Karo Regency in North Sumatra have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid areas surrounding Mount Sinabung following its eruption on Monday, which disrupted flights and prompted the evacuation of more than 2,400 residents.
In a statement on Tuesday, the Consulate General of Malaysia in Medan urged Malaysians to follow instructions issued by the Indonesian authorities, saying several flights at Medan's Kualanamu International Airport, a key gateway to North Sumatra, had reportedly been rescheduled or cancelled due to volcanic ash.
"Those travelling to or from Medan by air should contact their respective airlines directly for the latest information on any flight delays, rescheduling or cancellations," it said in a statement posted on its social media account on Tuesday.
Mount Sinabung erupted at 10.17am local time on Monday, spewing a thick column of volcanic ash about 3.5km above its summit, according to Indonesia's Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG).
Following the eruption, Indonesia's Geological Agency raised Mount Sinabung's status from Level II (Alert) to Level III (Standby) at 12.30pm after visual and instrumental monitoring showed increased volcanic activity.
The consulate said Indonesian authorities had also ordered the evacuation of 2,451 residents from nearby villages as a precautionary measure, while residents and visitors were advised to avoid activities within a 3km radius of the summit and within 6km of the south-southeast sector.
The consulate said it would continue to monitor the situation closely and provide updates should there be any significant developments.
Malaysians affected or requiring consular assistance may contact the consulate by telephone : +62 823 6164 6046 or by email : mwmedan@kln.gov.my.

Title: Melaka to subsidise motorcycle servicing for over 3,000 p-hailing riders
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Melaka will introduce a motorcycle maintenance subsidy to ease the financial burden of over 3,000 p-hailing delivery riders across the state.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the allocation will be tabled at the State Executive Council (Exco) meeting this week and announced next week.
"The subsidy will involve selected motorcycle repair workshops appointed in each state constituency. This will help p-hailing workers access maintenance services at lower rates.
"Delivery riders who send their motorcycles for service will receive a subsidy of 20 to 30 per cent off the total cost. Their welfare remains a priority for the state government, and this initiative aligns with the Melaka Sayang Rakyat (MeSRa) concept," he said.
Ab Rauf said the initiative is part of the state government's efforts to appreciate p-hailing workers, who play a vital role in facilitating the community's daily affairs through digital platforms.
He spoke to reporters after going to the ground to gain first-hand experience of p-hailing riders' daily lives by becoming a food delivery rider around Pengkalan Balak and Masjid Tanah town today.
The Chief Minister added that he took orders and delivered goods today to better understand the challenges and routines of riders striving to earn a living for their families.
"We will announce the registration process for qualified workshops alongside service providers such as Grab, Foodpanda, and Shopee later," he said.
Ab Rauf also said that the state government is exploring ways to expand Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for p-hailing workers to enhance their welfare protection.
He said the digital economy has transformed lifestyles, business methods, and employment patterns, making p-hailing a crucial sector within the digital economy ecosystem.
"It is good. The digital world is evolving, times are changing, lifestyles are changing, and business methods and the economy are transforming.
"Therefore, I take all these into account, resolve to address them, and will review studies I conducted to assist those working to support their families through p-hailing," he said.
Ab Rauf said efforts to strengthen the p-hailing ecosystem align with the vision to establish Melaka as a digital state, which includes implementing an official addressing system in village areas that currently lack formal addresses.
He said this is essential to enhance the government's service delivery system and match the efficiency of delivery systems run by p-hailing service providers.
Meanwhile, Ab Rauf invited the entire p-hailing community in the state to attend a special gathering in conjunction with the Youth Carnival at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, on Sept 4. On offer will be various lucky draw prizes, including 10 motorcycles and limited-edition helmets autographed by him.

Title: [UPDATED] Former minister arrested over Tabung Haji RCI probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former minister in connection with its probe into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's (RCI) report into Tabung Haji (TH).
The man, in his 60s, was believed to have been arrested at about 4.30pm today after turning up to give his statement at the MACC headquarters here.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest.
"The case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
"The suspect will be brought to the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court tomorrow morning for a remand application," he said.
Section 16(a)(A) deals with taking or seeking a bribe in exchange for favouring someone in a deal or transaction.
The offence is punishable under Section 24 of the same Act with up to 20 years' jail and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification involved, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The MACC has made a slew of high-profile arrests over the TH RCI report's findings.
Last week, it detained and obtained a week-long remand for
two former senior officials
, including a former TH chairman, as part of its investigation.
The other person detained was a former Treasury secretary-general.
Lawyer Datuk Seri K. Kumarendran, representing
former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Dr Mohd Irwan Serigar
Abdullah, had previously said there were no adverse inferences or findings against his client in the RCI report.
Lawyer Datuk M.M. Athimulan, who is acting for former TH chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, had said that the former auditor-general had publicly announced that there was no misappropriation and no theft.
MACC had also previously detained and summoned seven people to assist in the probe, including a former chief executive officer of a shipping company, a construction company director, a former company director and four senior ex-TH management personnel.
The RCI report, completed in 2022 after examining TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020, was declassified and made public on July 29, four years after the commission completed its work.
The RCI found serious weaknesses in TH's governance, financial management and investment decisions. Among others, it found that TH should have recorded a RM1.4 billion net loss in 2017, rather than the RM3.4 billion profit reported, and that hibah had been paid between 2014 and 2017 despite liabilities exceeding assets.
The report had also
raised concerns
over risky investments, excessive bonuses, conflicts of interest and weak disciplinary action against senior officers.
The RCI put forward 25 key recommendations including a major governance overhaul, tighter board appointment criteria, barring active politicians from the board, forensic audits of questionable investments and clearer separation of responsibility for haj affairs and financial management.
MACC has since said it was considering engaging external forensic experts to assist in examining documents and other evidence.

Title: Pahang Sultan, Tengku Ampuan extend condolences to families of four killed in 11-vehicle crash
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, and the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, have conveyed their condolences to the families of the victims killed in the accident involving 11 vehicles on the eastbound East Coast Expressway (LPT) in Lanchang, Temerloh, yesterday.
According to a Pahang Sultanate Facebook post, Their Royal Highnesses expressed their sympathy to the victims' families during this difficult time following the tragedy.
"Their Royal Highnesses pray that their souls will be placed among the faithful, while their families be given strength and fortitude in coping with their loss," Their Royal Highnesses said.
Meanwhile, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail also expressed his condolences to the family of the three family members who were killed in the accident.
He said the loss of Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, his wife Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan and their son Muhammad Armaan Nazeef in the blink of an eye had certainly left the entire family with great sadness and sorrow.
"May Allah shower His mercy upon their souls, forgive their sins and place them among His righteous," he said.
Nazatul and Nur Atiqah Sofiya, both 32, and their four-year-old son Muhammad Armaan Nazeef were among
four people killed in the accident
.
The other fatality was Honda CR-V passenger Seow Beng Wain, 55, from Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Selangor.

Title: Vstecs exits Isatec in RM48.75mil deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vstecs Bhd is disposing of its entire 40 per cent stake in Isatec Sdn Bhd to Singapore-based Skyform Pte Ltd for RM48.75 million, nearly 2.6 times its original investment cost.
In a bourse filing, Vstecs said it had, together with four management shareholders of Isatec, entered into a share purchase agreement with Skyform to dispose of a combined 75 per cent stake in Isatec for RM91.41 million.
Vstecs will receive RM48.75 million for its 233,334 shares, while the four management shareholders will collectively receive RM42.66 million for their 35 per cent stake.
Upon completion, Vstecs will cease to have any equity interest in Isatec, which will consequently cease to be its associate company.
The transaction is expected to be completed by the first quarter of 2027, subject to the fulfilment or waiver of conditions under the agreement.
Vstecs plans to use RM45.9 million, or 94.15 per cent of its disposal proceeds, for working capital within 12 months.
The company said the RM48.75 million consideration represents a 103.63 per cent premium over the RM23.94 million carrying value of its Isatec investment as at Dec 31, 2025, and a 159.31 per cent premium over its original investment cost of RM18.80 million.
Based on its latest audited financial statements, the disposal is expected to result in a one-off pro forma gain of about RM21.96 million, or 2.05 sen per share.
The gain is expected to raise Vstecs' net assets per share to about 53 sen from 51 sen on a pro forma basis.
Including RM16.22 million in cumulative dividends received from Isatec since the investment was completed in 2019 through December 2025, Vstecs' total cash returns would amount to about RM64.97 million.
This represents about 3.46 times its original investment cost over the roughly seven-year holding period.
Vstecs said the disposal would allow it to redirect capital towards its core businesses, particularly its ICT Distribution, Enterprise Systems and ICT Services segments.
Its ICT Services revenue has grown more than tenfold to RM454.45 million in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY25), from RM39.86 million in FY18, before its investment in Isatec.
The ICT Services and Enterprise Systems segments recorded revenue growth of 42.74 per cent and 29.88 per cent respectively in FY25.
Isatec, incorporated in 1994, provides software products and contract programming services related to information and communications technology for the corporate, financial and public sectors.
Skyform is a Singapore-incorporated company specialising in enterprise digital and artificial intelligence transformation services.
It is backed by SeaTown Private Capital Master Fund, a private equity fund managed by SeaTown Holdings International Pte Ltd, which is owned by Seviora Holdings, Temasek's main asset management platform.
Vstecs chief executive officer JH Soong said Isatec had grown and scaled well during the investment period.
"Our investment in Isatec was originally intended to strengthen the group's ICT Services segment. Since then, we have also built and significantly expanded our in-house ICT Services capabilities, with segment revenue increasing more than tenfold since 2018," he said.
"We believe the investment has achieved its original strategic objectives and it is now time to redeploy the capital into our wholly-owned core businesses, which continue to experience robust growth," he added.

Title: Ringgit ends lower after US Fed hints at rate hike
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the greenback on the first trading day of September on rising expectations of a US interest rate hike after Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's recent speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium.
At 6pm, the ringgit fell to 4.0370/0410 against the US dollar from last Friday's close of 4.0230/0270.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium last Friday has had a significant impact on the currencies market.
"Markets are focusing on his concern over inflation which would imply that the monetary tightening is almost inevitable in the near term, especially during the Federal Open Market Committee's two-day meeting beginning Sept 15," he said.
The Jackson Hole symposium, which ran from Aug 27-29, was closely watched by investors for clues on the Fed's next move on interest rates.
Mohd Afzanizam noted that the ringgit depreciated by 0.32 per cent to RM4.0398 today while other Asean currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also lower by 0.12 per cent, 0.31 per cent  and 0.18 per cent against the US dollar, respectively.
"Hence, the upcoming data point such as the ISM Manufacturing Index which will be published tonight will be closely monitored. Consensus estimates pegged the ISM index to be at 55.2 points in August versus 55.6 points in July," he added.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit appreciated against the euro to 4.6801/6847 from 4.6828/6874 last Friday but weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5223/5250 from 2.5193/5219.
It dipped against the British pound to 5.4657/4711 from 5.4632/4687.
The local note traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1703/1736 from 3.1652/1686 last Friday, slipped against the Philippine peso to 6.47/6.48 from 6.46/6.47 and gained against the Thai baht to 12.1315/1483 from 12.2087/2253.
The ringgit was also traded marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.5/227.8 compared with 227.3/227.7 previously.

Title: 'Hoping for a miracle': Hani refuses to give up on husband caught in Nepal floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "I am still positive and hoping for a miracle," said Hani Othman, whose husband remains among the Malaysians uncontactable following the Nepal floods.
Hani, who travelled to Kathmandu to seek updates on the search for her husband, senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, said she did not know how long she would remain in Nepal.
"Not sure yet," she told the New Straits Times when asked how long she planned to stay.
She said the aid supplies she had bought for flood victims were ready, but she was still waiting for approval to bring them into the affected area.
In the meantime, she had started sending
essential items
through a Nepalese non-governmental organisation (NGO) for distribution to victims today.
She also asked the NGO to help search for her husband and his team in the affected area.
Hani had earlier mobilised public support to collect essential supplies for flood victims, eventually filling a lorry with donations.
She had hoped the effort would also allow her to join a volunteer team heading to a survivors' camp, where she could continue looking for Fakhrul Munir, 44, a member of the Fire and Rescue Department's Special Air Operations Team.
Affectionately known as Loe, he was among 17 Malaysians travelling together in Rasuwa district when flash floods struck the area.
The group has remained uncontactable, with rescue efforts hampered by damaged roads and disrupted communications in the mountainous area.

Title: Serian tops API at 374, no monitoring station records 'good' air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today.
Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Serian police headquarters recording the nation's highest API reading at 374, followed by Kuching (346), Sarikei (333), Sibu (323) and Samarahan (318).
Four locations in Sarawak recorded "very unhealthy" API readings between 201 and 300, with Sri Aman recording 295, Bintulu (247), Mukah (241) and Samalaju (226).
11 locations recorded "unhealthy" readings between 101 and 200, including four in Sarawak.
These were ILP Miri (191), Miri (186), Kapit (185), Limbang, Sarawak (173), Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (177), and Labuan (171).
Four locations in Sabah recorded unhealthy readings: Kimanis (165), Keningau (165), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (161) and Tawau (154).
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded an unhealthy reading of 157.
Meanwhile, 48 locations recorded "moderate" API readings between 51 and 100.
No monitoring station recorded "good" air quality.

Title: Dunham-Bush invests RM172mil in Negri Sembilan expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd will invest approximately RM172 million in the first phase of a new manufacturing facility at SPD Tech Valley in Senawang, Negri Sembilan.
The global manufacturer of heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC/R) solutions signed a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) with SPD Tech Valley Sdn Bhd for approximately 32 acres of industrial land at the industrial park.
The SPA was signed by Dunham-Bush Industries Sdn Bhd managing director Yu Boashuang and Seri Pajam Development Group chief executive officer Ten Wee Seong, who represented SPD Tech Valley, at Park Hyatt, Kuala Lumpur on Aug 28.
The signing ceremony was witnessed by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Also present were Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital Affairs state executive councillor Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Invest Negri Sembilan chief executive officer Datuk Najmuddin Sharif Sarimon and Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) Negri Sembilan director Azizul Hakim Abu Haniffa.
RM172 MILLION EXPANSION
The Phase 1 development is expected to create up to 400 job opportunities, including skilled and technical positions.
Construction is targeted to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with operations expected to commence in the first quarter of 2028.
The new facility will strengthen Dunham-Bush's manufacturing capacity for chiller systems and advanced HVAC/R solutions, serving both Malaysian and international markets.
The expansion is also expected to create wider opportunities for local suppliers, engineering services, logistics providers and other supporting industries.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH
Dunham-Bush's expansion at SPD Tech Valley adds to industrial investment within the Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0) corridor and supports Negri Sembilan's efforts to attract quality investments with greater economic and technological value.
The project also highlights the role of Invest Negri Sembilan, MIDA and relevant government agencies in facilitating investments and supporting companies looking to expand in the state.
Ten said Dunham-Bush's presence would complement the growing industrial ecosystem at SPD Tech Valley.
"We are honoured to welcome Dunham-Bush to SPD Tech Valley. With its longstanding engineering expertise and international presence, the company brings valuable manufacturing capabilities that will complement the industrial ecosystem we are building," he said.
SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
Developed by Seri Pajam Development Group, SPD Tech Valley is a 523-acre smart, managed and sustainable industrial park in Senawang, Negri Sembilan, within the MVV 2.0 development corridor.
The park is Southeast Asia's first LEED Gold-certified industrial park, combining sustainable planning, smart infrastructure and integrated industrial services.
It offers ready-built factories and built-to-suit industrial land, supported by high-capacity utilities and access to Malaysia's national power infrastructure.
Strategically connected to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Port Klang, the North-South Expressway and the Lekas Highway, the park provides manufacturers with access to key logistics gateways and regional markets.
SPD Tech Valley is attracting companies across the semiconductor, electrical and electronics (E&E), manufacturing and new energy sectors, as well as other high-value industries, with several investors progressing with their development plans.
The addition of Dunham-Bush further strengthens the park's growing industrial ecosystem and its position as a strategic manufacturing base for Malaysia and regional markets.

Title: Vulnerable groups urged to avoid outdoor activities as Sabah haze hits 4 areas
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has advised vulnerable groups to avoid outdoor activities following unhealthy air quality recorded in several areas of the state.
The Media and Communications Office of the Sabah Chief Minister's Department said four areas recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with Kota Kinabalu recording the highest at 177, followed by Kimanis at 166, Keningau at 165 and Tawau at 153.
It said children, senior citizens, pregnant women and individuals with respiratory problems should also avoid strenuous and physically demanding activities.
"Those who need to be outdoors are advised to wear suitable face masks, drink sufficient water and maintain personal hygiene after outdoor activities," it said.
Those experiencing symptoms such as coughing, breathing difficulties or chest pain are advised to seek treatment at the nearest health facility.
The public is also advised to ensure good ventilation indoors to reduce exposure to polluted air.
The JPBN also reminded the public to avoid open burning and regularly monitor API readings, as well as the latest advisories from the Department of Environment (DOE) and health authorities.
The committee said it would continue monitoring air quality throughout the state and urged the public to take precautionary measures to reduce health risks arising from exposure to polluted air.

Title: Reducing Indonesia wildfires will be challenging as El Nino peaks this month, minister warns
Article:
JAKARTA: Efforts to reduce wildfires ablaze across Indonesia will be challenging as the El Nino weather phenomenon will peak this month, the forestry minister said on Tuesday, describing the devastation as largely man-made.
Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from forest and land fires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands.
The haze has caused respiratory illnesses and forced thousands of schools to move classes online, including in neighbouring Malaysia.
The "super-El Nino" weather conditions exacerbate the fires, causing drought.
Hot spots were reduced across Kalimantan and Sumatra by the end of August, minister Raja Juli Antoni said.
"Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Nino," he said. "September is the main fight for us."
The haze caused more than 50,000 cases of acute respiratory infection across seven provinces between July and August, health ministry official Andi Saguni said on Tuesday.
Winds blows haze to surrounding provinces and cause infections in places without wildfires, Andi added.
Wildfires burned about 200,000 hectares of land from January to July, forestry ministry data showed, increasing from 107,465 burned hectares from January to June.
Raja Juli said the fires were in large part deliberately set, either by individuals or corporations.
Despite crackdowns, burning forests to clear land for agriculture and other economic activities has been a common practice in Indonesia. Borneo has vast stretches of peatland where fire can smoulder underground for weeks.
Six forestry permit holders have been fined and the ministry has said a criminal probe was possible.
Satellite imaging has revealed that 42 companies hold concessions with high wildfire potential, senior environment ministry official Rizal Irawan said on Monday.
Authorities used weather modification to trigger rain and have "water bombed" areas to contain the hot spots and mitigate the fires, Raja Juli said.
The Philippines said haze blanketed the capital Manila on Tuesday, pushing air quality to "very unhealthy" and "acutely unhealthy" levels in some areas.
The air quality in six areas in Malaysia's state of Sarawak reached hazardous levels on Tuesday, data from Malaysia's environmental department showed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 262 motorcycles inspected, 155 summonses issued in Klang, Kuala Selangor operations
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A total of 262 motorcyclists were inspected, with 155 summonses issued for various traffic offences in two operations, codenamed Op Samseng Jalanan and Op Bersepadu Ambang Merdeka in Kuala Selangor and Klang respectively yesterday.
Kuala Selangor district police chief Supt Azaharudin Tajuddin said the operation, which began around 4pm and focused on Pantai Remis, Jeram, was conducted following the detection of a gathering spot for motorcyclists to showcase stunts and modified exhausts.
The seven-hour operation resulted in the inspection of 140 vehicles, with 90 summonses issued for various traffic violations, in addition to the seizure of five motorcycles.
"The detected offences included the absence of driving licence, insurance coverage, registration number and rearview mirror, not wearing a helmet, modifying the exhaust, and not displaying L or P stickers, in addition to other traffic violations," he said when contacted today.
Meanwhile, Klang South district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said that in an operation on Persiaran Raja Muda Musa, Klang, a total of 122 motorcyclists were inspected and 65 traffic summonses were issued.
He said in the operation which began at 12.01am, his team also seized 21 motorcycles for further action.
Among the detected offences were driving without a licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licence, registration number violations, exhaust modifications, as well as vehicle structure and accessory issues.
"Additionally, two individuals were detained to assist in the investigation under Section 45A(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 related to the offence of driving or riding under the influence of alcohol," he also said.
He added that the operation conducted until 6.30am was an effort to ensure the safety and smooth flow of traffic throughout the National Day Eve celebrations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: MOH monitoring URT, conjunctivitis cases
Article:
SIBU: The Health Ministry (MOH) is monitoring the increase in cases of acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis in Sarawak following the haze conditions affecting several areas in the state.
Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said continuous monitoring is being carried out through health facilities including health clinics and hospitals to ensure that any increase in cases related to the haze can be dealt with immediately.
She said based on monitoring by the Sarawak State Health Department, the average URTI cases increased from about 1,717 cases per week at the beginning of the year to 1,752 cases per week recently.
Conjunctivitis cases have also increased from an average of about 17 to 21 cases per week, while overall asthma activity remains stable at the state level.
"MOH is constantly monitoring the current situation including the trend of patient arrivals at health facilities and we want to ensure that facilities and health workers are prepared in case of an increase in cases due to the haze," she said.
She said this when met during a visit to the Jalan Oya Health Clinic here today in conjunction with the Borneo Health Tour Series 4, which also focused on the Ministry of Health's preparedness in dealing with health situations related to haze.
Hanifah said the public, especially at-risk groups such as children, the elderly and those with respiratory problems, needed to take precautions when the air quality was at unhealthy levels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India busts firm faking expiry dates, nutrition labels on PepsiCo, Nestle food exports
Article:
MUMBAI: Indian authorities have raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo, Nestle, Coca-Cola and Unilever so they could be exported to other countries.
Reuters got exclusive access to the warehouse last week as food officers conducted a six-day investigation and seized goods worth nearly US$80,000.
A photographer saw chemicals used to remove manufacturers' original expiry dates and ingredient labels, machines to print and apply replacements and scores of label packs for products including Lay's potato chips and Maggi noodles.
India's Maharashtra state, where Mumbai is the capital, has intensified a food safety drive under the new head of the state's Food and Drug Administration, Tukaram Mundhe, whose surprise inspections at elite clubs and restaurants have made him an online and TV celebrity.
"I am absolutely shocked by the scale. It is like organised activity. It's been done systematically," Mundhe told Reuters on Tuesday about the investigation into the illicit warehouse operation.
The warehouse, located in the industrial area of Navi Mumbai around 25 km  from Mumbai's international airport, was run by privately owned Sadhana Enterprises.
Its owner said they carried out the activities on behalf of 19 little-known exporters, according to a media release from the state and a police case document.
Officials said most products were expired or near expired.
By changing dates, "harmful food products are being exported for sale, thereby defrauding customers," the case document said.
It was not clear which countries the products were destined for but all the stock was for export, Mundhe said. At least one reprinted label on a PepsiCo packet was in English and French, Reuters found.
PepsiCo, Nestle, Unilever India unit Hindustan Unilever , and Coca-Cola did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.
Reuters calls to warehouse co-owners Jayprakash Sanchatiram Singh and Jaya Navrang Bahadur Singh were not answered. It was not clear whether any arrests had been made.
The gated warehouse had four large rooms beneath a tin roof.
Officials found nearly 5,000 cartons of consumer products, including PepsiCo's Lay's and Kurkure chips, Nestle's Maggi Masala Noodles, Unilever's Knorr Mushroom Soup and Hellmann's Mayonnaise, and Coca-Cola's Thums Up and Limca cans.
Many of the Kurkure and Maggi packets, as well as the Thums Up cans, had their dates removed.
Inside the dirty warehouse, Reuters photographer Francis Mascarenhas saw a can of a chemical solvent that officials said was used to erase dates from the packets.
[[nid:1523619]]
They said an operator would enter the fake expiry and manufacturing dates using a stylus on a computer screen.
Workers would then use a machine fitted to a metal table, decorated with a tiny "I love my India" sticker, to allegedly print the new label on packaging and cans.
"The original date of manufacture and expiry date on the packaging of the food articles had been scratched out, erased ... (and) new information printed over them," the police document said.
The police case did not accuse any global companies of wrongdoing, but Mundhe called for supply chain accountability.
"Everybody needs to take this seriously. Companies have to abide with compliances and ensure that branding, packaging and sale is done as per regulations," he said.
Enforcement of food safety laws is weak in India.
Food safety checks have long focused on adulteration, particularly of dairy products, when cases rise during festive seasons as demand for traditional Indian sweets surges.
Mundhe told Reuters his team found some packs were being reprinted with a future manufacturing date of October 2, 2026 inside the Mumbai warehouse.
Given foreign countries may have different labelling requirements and health guidelines, Reuters found dozens of Maggi cartons in the warehouse, with one sample showing a fake nutrition label pasted on top of a pack, making it export ready by describing it as a "Product of India."
One PepsiCo Kurkure pack had a nutrition label in English and French in a bilingual format.
The fake label reduced the quantity of cereal products in its ingredients by 10 per cent, and tweaked the number of calories and serving size in an apparent move to align the labels with foreign regulations.

Title: Agrobank to fully disburse RM200mil under oil palm smallholder scheme by October
Article:
SERDANG: Bank Pertanian Malaysia Bhd (Agrobank) aims to fully utilise RM200 million in financing for oil palm smallholders under the TSPKS 2.0 replanting scheme by October this year.
Agrobank has so far approved 4,380 applications worth RM190.99 million, group president and group chief executive officer Datuk Tengku Ahmad Badli Shah Raja Hussin said.
"We are targeting RM200 million to be fully financed by October this year," he said after the launch of the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0 system today.
The system, jointly developed by Agrobank and the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), is designed to streamline applications and monitoring under the scheme.
It allows MPOB officers to upload information and supporting documents gathered during site visits, including photographs of plantations, for financing assessment.
The system was launched by Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition 2026.
The scheme provides funding comprising a 50 per cent grant and 50 per cent financing to eligible independent oil palm smallholders to replant old or less productive trees.
It is open to smallholders with oil palm holdings of up to 4.047 hectares.
Tengku Ahmad Badli said the government could provide additional funding for the scheme next year, subject to Finance Ministry approval.
He said the same digital platform could be used should additional funding be approved, allowing applications to be monitored throughout the financing process.
"Through this system, if there is additional funding approved in the future, the same application will be used so that the entire financing process can be monitored.
"Every application can be monitored end-to-end, from submission until the financing is disbursed," he said.
TSPKS 2.0 builds on the TSPKS 1.0 programme and is implemented through a collaboration between the Plantation and Commodities Ministry, MPOB and Agrobank.
The initiative is aimed at helping independent smallholders undertake replanting in a more planned manner while improving productivity, farm resilience and long-term income.
